In no event will the Third Judicial Circuit be held liable to any party for any damages arising in any way out of the availability, use, reliance on or inability to use this website or any information provided by or through the Third Judicial Circuit website, or for any claim attributable to errors, omissions or other inaccuracies in the Third Judicial Circuit website.\n\nNotice to the public\n\nThe Code of Judicial Conduct governing behavior by judges forbids judges from discussing pending cases with the public or parties to cases. Please do not call the Court expecting to speak with a judge about any case. The Court is only allowed to consider evidence and arguments made in the courtroom and in documents properly filed by actual parties in the case as authorized by law and the Rules of Court. The Court cannot ethically read or consider any other evidence or arguments about the case.  Ex parte communications also applies to the General Magistrate & Hearing Officers.\n\nF.S. 668.6076\n\nUnder Florida law, e-mail addresses are public records. If you do not want your e-mail address released in response to a public records request, do not send electronic mail to this entity. Instead, contact the Court by phone or in writing.\n\nPowered by Translate\nFlorida SCS Title VI Anti-Retaliation Policy\n\nIt is the policy of Florida State Courts System (SCS) to comply with Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, as amended.  The SCS does not and will not exclude from participation in, deny the benefits of, or subject anyone to discrimination on the basis of race, color, or national origin.  Please click this link for more details.\n\n© All rights reserved\nCourt Staff are prohibited from providing legal advice. 408\nLake City, FL 32055\n\nPhilip Fowler\n\nTrial Court Administrator\n\nPhone: (386) 758-2164\nFax: (386) 758-2162\n\nADA Accommodation Request Form\nADA Grievance Procedure (AO 2014-009)\n\nThe Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, prohibits discrimination on the basis of disability in state and local government services. This includes participation in court proceedings. Pursuant to Title II of the ADA the Florida State Courts System will make reasonable modifications in policies, practices and procedures; furnish auxiliary aids and services; and afford program accessibility.\n\nParties, witnesses, lawyers, jurors and other court participants can request assistance with things such as large print documents, American Sign Language interpreters, assistive listening devices, assignment to wheelchair accessible court rooms, and the like.\n\nPursuant to Rule 2.540 Florida Rules of General Practice and Judicial Administration – All notices of court proceedings to be held in a public facility, and all process compelling appearance at such proceedings, shall include the statement immediately below in bold face, 14-point Times New Roman or Courier font.\n\nIf you are a person with a disability who needs an accommodation in order to participate in this proceeding, you are entitled, at no cost to you, to the provision of certain assistance. Please contact Court Administration, 173 NE Hernando Avenue, Room 408, Lake City, Florida 32055; (386)758-2163 or complete the ADA Request form located at https://thirdcircuitfl.org/ada-accommodation-request/ at least 7 days before your scheduled court appearance, or immediately upon receiving this notification if the time before the scheduled appearance is less than 7 days; if you are hearing or voice impaired call 711.\n\nPress Escape to close the search panel.\nX Feed | Circuit3FL\n\nJudge Kathryn R. Help\nFacebook-f\n \nX-twitter\nIMPORTANT COURT AND WEATHER ALERTS\nCivil Law\nHelpful Informational Video On The Procedures Of Small Claims Court\nPROCESS SERVER INFORMATION\n\nAnyone interested in becoming a certified process server in the Third Judicial Circuit should carefully review this information page, Administrative Order No. 2026-006, and the application packet.\n\nThe current contact information for Court Administration in the Third Judicial Circuit:\n\nColumbia County Courthouse\n173 NE Hernando Avenue, RM 408\nLake City, Florida 32055\nPhone: (386) 754-7107\n\nDesignated Employee: Lisa Butler, Human Resources Analyst II\n\nFees and Method of Payment:\nThe initial certification fee is $100.00. The renewal certification fee is $75.00.    These fees are nonrefundable and are due each year upon initial certification or renewal.\nThe certification fee must be paid by cashier’s check or money order and made out to “State of Florida”.\nThe applicant will need to provide an annual criminal history background investigation through FDLE at the applicant’s expense. The following is the FDLE website: http://www.fdle.state.fl.us/. (Request criminal history) The certified results must be mailed to Lisa Butler at the mailing address above.\nNew civil process server applicants are required to complete a class and exam through The Florida Association of Professional Process Servers (FAPPS.) The website is as follows: https://www.fapps.org/afpscourseschedule.aspx Here you will find the dates and times that classes are available. For new applicants, the 16-hour course will be mandatory, and for annual renewals, the 4-hour continuing education course will be mandatory. Both are available to be taken by Zoom.\nA completed application packet should include (1) the four-page application, (2) the Statement of Policy Regarding Conduct of Certified Process Servers, (3) the Certified Process Server Agreement, (4) the Certificate of Good Conduct, and (5) the certification fee.\nFor new certifications, the applicant can mail, or hand deliver to the address listed above, the following application materials: application, certification fee and passport photos. (Certified results from the FDLE criminal background history must be mailed to Lisa Butler at the mailing address above)\nOnce a new applicant has completed their FAPPS class, the certificate needs to be forwarded to this office along with a Bond naming “Administrative Office of the Courts, Third Judicial Circuit” as the Obligee in the amount of $5,000.00. When all required documents have been submitted, the certified civil process server will be sworn in, and a badge and an order signed by the Chief Judge will be issued.\nFor annual renewals, each civil process server must submit the renewal fee, updated bond, updated passport photo, yearly FDLE background investigation report and proof of the required 4-hour continuing education course from FAPPS.\nIf you have any questions about the Certified Process Server Program, please direct those questions to Lisa Butler, at the address or phone number listed above.\nCERTIFIED PROCESS SERVERS\nPROCESS SERVER APPLICATION\nCIVIL CASE MANAGERS\n\nDixie County\n\nSasha Patten\n\nCivil Case Manager\n\n4424 NW American Lane, Suite 102\n\nLake City, Florida 32055\n\n(386) 754-7040\n\npatten.sasha@jud3.flcourts.org\n\nColumbia County\n\nHamilton County\n\nMegan Gutshall\n\n4424 NW American Lane, Suite 102\n\nLake City, Florida 32055\n\n(386) 719-7577\n\ngutshall.megan@jud3.flcourts.org\n\nLafayette County\nMadison County\nTaylor County\nSuwannee County\n\nAmber Hancock\n\n4424 NW American Lane, Suite 102\n\nLake City, Florida 32055\n\n(386) 719-1467\n\nhancock.amber@jud3.flcourts.org\n\n \n\n\n\n\n\nPress Escape to close the search panel.\nX Feed | Circuit3FL\n\nJudge Kathryn R. Please do not call the Court expecting to speak with a judge about any case.
